name: SpaceX
day_summary: Day 4 of trading. SPCX is recovering in early session/premarket to ~$208.24 after Tuesday's extraordinary session: the stock hit an intraday ATH of $225.64 (briefly overtaking Microsoft to become the world's fourth-largest stock) before plunging back to close at $201.80 (+4.83% from the $192.50 Day 2 close). The June 16 session confirmed that the $190–$200 pullback entry zone from the brief was briefly touched (intraday low $195.13) and then blew through on the recovery — the entry window was real, instantaneous, and extremely difficult to execute. Two key catalysts emerged June 16: SpaceX confirmed deployment of all three Bluebird satellites for AST SpaceMobile (Falcon 9 mission operational success signal), and SPCX stock surged past analyst consensus as a Cursor AI deal emerged (AI pivot signal). Day 4 premarket at $208.24 is +3.2% from Tuesday's close, with FOMC at 2:30 PM ET as the macro gate.
long_pnl: +53.5% from the $135 IPO offer (from $201.80 Day 3 close); IPO allocants up ~$66.80/share; Day 3 holders at $201.80 up ~+3.2% premarket to $208.24
short_pnl: −3.2% premarket from the $201.80 Day 3 close — options market now 1 day old; put/call infrastructure is building but spreads still wide; defined-risk bears are building positions slowly

decision.rationale: HOLD/WAIT at low conviction. The June 16 intraday low of $195.13 touched the $190–$200 pullback entry zone identified in prior briefs, but the entry required perfect timing that almost no retail participant could execute — the low was a brief wick before the stock launched back above $200. Day 4 at $208.24 is still above any prior identified entry zone. Options market is now 1 day old; spreads are narrowing from the debut-day 80–90% IV but are not yet tight enough for standard retail hedging. The MSCI passive bid is ongoing and the float/squeeze dynamic remains. Discipline: do not chase $208 on Day 4. If FOMC brings volatility and SPCX pulls to $195–$200 again, that is the defined entry with a put hedge (once spreads allow). IPO allocants: continue trimming into strength, hold a reduced core.

positioning.iv_note: Front-week IV has compressed to ~65–70% (from debut-day 80–90%) as Day 2 of the options market builds positioning. Bid-ask spreads on near-term strikes are narrowing (now estimated 1.5–3 points vs 2–5 points on Day 1). In 1–2 more sessions, protective puts become a viable hedging instrument for a new-money entry at $195–$200.
positioning.short_interest: minimal borrow — options market now 1 day old; put buyers are starting to establish risk-defined bearish positions but short interest in the traditional sense remains negligible; the $195–$200 strike put activity is building
positioning.max_pain: ~$195 (June 20 expiry based on first-day options OI; will shift as OI builds)
positioning.notable_flow: Day 2 of the SPCX options market. The dominant June 16 flow was speculative call buying (momentum chasers buying the $210–$220 strikes that got briefly touched intraday). Day 4 is seeing the first organized put-buying from institutional risk managers establishing defined-risk shorts for the first time since the IPO. The IV compression from 85% to 65–70% is the structural signal to watch: when IV reaches 55–60% and spreads normalize to <1 point on near-term at-the-money strikes, the hedged entry at $195–$200 becomes mechanically viable. That window is likely 2–3 sessions out — Thursday or Monday.

what_traders_are_doing: Day 4 transition dynamics. Momentum desks who rode the June 16 rip from $192.50 to $225.64 and held through the close at $201.80 are watching the FOMC event risk with caution: a hawkish Warsh could be the trigger that finally exhausts the MSCI passive bid and produces the real $185–$195 pullback that was never achieved in Days 1–3. IPO allocants continue trimming into strength at $205–$210. The options market participants are building risk — this is the first session where defined-risk bearish positions (puts) are being established at scale. The Week 2 narrative begins: the story transitions from 'record IPO float squeeze' to 'options market discovery' as OI builds and the delta-hedging dynamic begins to matter.

analysis:
## Day 4: recovering from a historic intraday reversal

SPCX is trading at **$208.24** in early Day 4, recovering from Tuesday's extraordinary session that combined a new all-time high of **$225.64** (briefly making SpaceX the world's fourth-largest company, overtaking Microsoft) with an intraday reversal of nearly $24 to close at **$201.80**. The June 16 session was the clearest single-day demonstration of what a ~4% float looks like at $2.2T market cap: violent in both directions, exhausting the momentum buyers, and landing at a price that is 'only' +4.83% from the day before.

## Two new catalysts from June 16

Beyond the price action, two fundamental developments emerged. [SpaceX confirmed the successful deployment of all three Bluebird satellites](https://coingape.com/spacex-confirms-deployment-of-all-3-bluebird-satellites-spcx-stock-gains/) for AST SpaceMobile — a Falcon 9 operational success that signals the growing small-sat economy SpaceX is infrastructure for. And [TechTimes reported a Cursor AI partnership deal](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318515/20260616/spacex-stock-surges-past-analyst-consensus-cursor-deal-signals-ai-pivot.htm) that broadens the investment narrative from 'launch + Starlink' to 'AI-embedded space infrastructure' — a new valuation layer the market was beginning to price when the stock briefly touched the $227 street-high analyst PT intraday.

## The $195.13 low: the entry zone was real

The June 16 intraday low of $195.13 touched the **$190–$200 pullback entry zone** identified in prior briefs. But executing that entry required catching a brief wick in a session where the stock had already traveled $30 from open to close. For most participants, the entry window was unactionable. Day 4 at $208 is above every prior identified entry zone. The discipline remains: **do not chase at $208**. The FOMC today could produce the second attempt at the $195–$200 zone. If spreads normalize to <1.5 points on near-term puts within the next 1–2 sessions, a hedged entry at that level becomes the defined-risk setup to wait for.
